body.heading: Trace your hands
paragraphs: Draw around your hands on paper, or ask your adult to help. Cut them out carefully — an adult can do the cutting for younger children.
You will have paper hands with five fingers each. Hands are perfect for this job, because hands are what we help with.

body.heading: Write your promises
paragraphs: On each paper hand, write or draw one way you can help: I can tidy my toys. I can water the plants. I can share my crayons.
Small promises are the best kind. A promise you can really keep is worth more than a giant promise you cannot.

body.heading: Hang the garland
paragraphs: Tape your hands along a string and hang it where everyone can see. Add hands from the whole family if they want to join.
Every time you keep a promise, draw a little star on that hand. Watch your garland fill with stars.

takeaway: A garland of paper hands shows all the small ways you can help, and stars mark the promises you kept.
safetyNotes: An adult should do or closely help with all cutting. Hang the garland where it will not fall on anyone.
screenFreeExtension: Choose one promise from the garland and do it today before bedtime.
